Tally flags into a loss table

Source: R/tally.R
tally_flags.Rd

Counts, per group, how many records each test flags and how many a cleaning rule removes. A rule is a set of tests: a record is removed when it carries any of them. Works on a flagged data frame or on the on-disk output of flag_occurrences(), which is streamed part by part.

Usage

tally_flags(x, by = NULL, rules = NULL, bins = NULL, tests = NULL)

Arguments

x

A data frame returned by flag_occurrences() (or any data frame with an integer flags column), an occ_flagged object, or its output directory.

by

Character vector of grouping columns. For on-disk output these must have been passed as keep when flagging. Missing values form the group "missing".

rules

Named list of character vectors of test names. Default: one rule, "all", holding every test present in the flags.

bins

Named list of numeric break points. Each named column is cut at those breaks into a factor-like character column <name>_bin (closed on the left, missing values labelled "missing") and added to by.

tests

Tests to count individually. Default: those recorded with the flags, or every test with a set bit.

Value

A data frame of class occ_tally with the by columns, n (records), n_valid (records without the invalid flag, when invalid was run), one column flagged_<test> per test, per rule removed_<rule> and kept_<rule>, and per rule and test of the rule only_<rule>_<test>: the records that test is the sole reason the rule removes. The attribute occ_rules holds the rules and occ_by the grouping columns. summary() turns the counts into percentages and plot() draws them.

Examples

x <- data.frame(species = c("a", "a", "b", "c"), kingdom = c("P", "P", "A", "A"),
                decimalLongitude = c(12.58, 0, 16.37, 2.35),
                decimalLatitude = c(55.67, 0, 48.21, 48.85))
f <- flag_occurrences(x, tests = c("invalid", "zero", "gbif_headquarters", "capital"))
tally_flags(f, by = "kingdom",
            rules = list(strict = c("zero", "gbif_headquarters", "capital"), mild = "zero"))
